stages.name: Trojanized MSI Installer
observables: MSI files impersonating PuTTy, WinSCP, Google Authenticator
Digitally signed MSI files to appear benign

stages.name: TextShell Packer Execution
observables: API hammering using irrelevant GDI calls (RevokeDragDrop, GetDC, CreateSolidBrush, SetMapMode)
IsDebuggerPresent() check leading to infinite loop 'while(1);'
Custom hashing formula for API resolution: h = (h * 0x2001 + ord(ch))
Allocation of RWX memory using NtAllocateVirtualMemory
Data copied in 8-byte chunks to allocated memory

stages.name: Shellcode LZMA Decompression
observables: Custom LZMA range decoder with parameters lc=3, lp=0, pb=2
Relocation fixups for relative CALL (E8) and JMP (E9) opcodes
VirtualProtect calls to change memory regions to executable

stages.name: Downloader Intermediate Stage
observables: HTTP communication to retrieve OysterLoader core
Environment verification (language check, keyboard layout identification)
Custom hashing for server communication parameters

stages.name: Payload Deployment (Vidar/Rhysida)
observables: Deployment of Vidar infostealer for credential theft
Execution of Rhysida ransomware for file encryption

scenario.summary: OysterLoader (Broomstick) is a multi-stage C++ loader distributed via trojanized installers for software like PuTTy and WinSCP. It utilizes the TextShell packer, custom LZMA decompression, and in-memory shellcode to eventually deliver Rhysida ransomware or Vidar infostealers.

meta.rationale: Focus on hosts with 'IT Tool' lures like PuTTy or WinSCP. Widen to the whole fleet if any branch returns malicious hits.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has used OysterLoader to deploy Vidar for credential harvesting or Rhysida for ransomware, evidenced by unauthorized access to browser data, .rhysida file creation, or proxy-based C2 traffic.

hunt.name: OysterLoader Impact: Vidar and Rhysida
hunt.description: This hunt isolates the final payload stage of the OysterLoader infection chain. It focuses on the behavioral signatures of Vidar (infostealer) and Rhysida (ransomware) once they have been unpacked and executed. The hunt identifies hosts at risk due to the presence of software OysterLoader typically impersonates (e.g., PuTTy, WinSCP) and then gathers parallel evidence of credential theft, anomalous processes, encryption activity, and multi-hop proxy connections (Tor).

nodes.label: Scope hosts with potentially trojanized software

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname, package_name, vendor_name, package_version FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE instr(',' || '{{impersonated_packages}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(package_name) || ',') > 0
config.description: Identify hosts running software OysterLoader frequently impersonates, narrowing the hunt to potential beachheads.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts with IT tools that may have been installed from trojanized sources. Silence means the specific impersonated tools are not present.

primitive_config.label: Scope hosts with potentially trojanized software
primitive_config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname, package_name, vendor_name, package_version FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE instr(',' || '{{impersonated_packages}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(package_name) || ',') > 0
primitive_config.expected: A list of hosts with IT tools that may have been installed from trojanized sources. Silence means the specific impersonated tools are not present.

nodes.label: Vidar: Non-browser access to browser credentials

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, file_path, COUNT(*) AS access_count FROM hb_file_activity WHERE activity_id = 2 AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\google\\chrome\\user data\\default\\login data%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\microsoft\\edge\\user data\\default\\login data%') AND LOWER(process_name) NOT LIKE '%chrome.exe' AND LOWER(process_name) NOT LIKE '%msedge.exe' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, process_name, file_path
config.description: Detect processes reading browser profile data, which is characteristic of Vidar credential harvesting (T1555).
config.expected_signal: A non-browser process reading 'Login Data'. Silence suggests no such credential theft occurred via file access.

primitive_config.label: Vidar: Non-browser access to browser credentials
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, file_path, COUNT(*) AS access_count FROM hb_file_activity WHERE activity_id = 2 AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\google\\chrome\\user data\\default\\login data%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\microsoft\\edge\\user data\\default\\login data%') AND LOWER(process_name) NOT LIKE '%chrome.exe' AND LOWER(process_name) NOT LIKE '%msedge.exe' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, process_name, file_path
primitive_config.expected: A non-browser process reading 'Login Data'. Silence suggests no such credential theft occurred via file access.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_name) AS process, process_file_company, on_disk, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (on_disk = 0 OR process_file_company IS NULL OR process_file_company = '') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 HAVING hosts <= 3 ORDER BY hosts ASC
config.description: Stack-count rare processes that are either fileless (injected) or lack standard company metadata, suggesting unpacked malware.
config.expected_signal: A process seen on very few hosts without proper metadata. Silence may indicate all processes are signed and on-disk.

primitive_config.label: Rare processes without valid signatures
primitive_config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_name) AS process, process_file_company, on_disk, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (on_disk = 0 OR process_file_company IS NULL OR process_file_company = '') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 HAVING hosts <= 3 ORDER BY hosts ASC
primitive_config.expected: A process seen on very few hosts without proper metadata. Silence may indicate all processes are signed and on-disk.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, COUNT(*) AS file_count FROM hb_file_activity WHERE (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%.rhysida' OR LOWER(file_name) = 'criticalid.txt') AND activity_id IN (1, 3, 5) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, process_name HAVING file_count >= {{encryption_threshold}}
config.description: Identify the sudden creation of .rhysida files or ransom notes (T1486).
config.expected_signal: A single process creating many files with the .rhysida extension. Silence means no mass encryption was observed.

nodes.label: C2 Analysis: Tor and multi-hop proxy ports

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, direction FROM hb_network_connection WHERE (dst_endpoint_ip = '127.0.0.1' AND dst_endpoint_port IN (9050, 9051, 1080)) OR (dst_endpoint_port IN (9001, 443) AND LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%tor%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Detect multi-hop proxy connections (T1090.003) commonly used by Rhysida/Vidar for C2.
config.expected_signal: Non-standard processes using local proxy ports or launching Tor. Silence suggests no proxy-based C2 within the window.
